title: Cumin Lamb Stir-Fry
description: Thin-sliced lamb seared hard in a smoking-hot wok with whole cumin seeds, dried chiles, and onions. A Xinjiang-inspired classic that delivers big flavor in under 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: dried red chiles
ingredients.notes: snipped in half, seeds shaken out if you want less heat

steps.text: Toss sliced lamb with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch. Set aside while you prep the vegetables — even 5 minutes of marinating helps.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Add 1 tablespoon oil, then spread the lamb in a single layer. Let it sear undisturbed until deeply browned on one side, about 2 minutes. Flip and cook 1 minute more. Transfer to a plate — it will finish cooking later.
Add remaining tablespoon of oil to the wok. Toss in cumin seeds and dried chiles, stirring until the cumin is fragrant and a shade darker, about 30 seconds.
Add onion and bell pepper. Stir-fry over high heat until slightly charred at the edges but still crisp, about 3 minutes.
Return the lamb and any juices to the wok. Add garlic and ground cumin. Toss everything together over high heat for 1 minute until the spices coat the meat and the garlic is fragrant.
Season with salt, taste, and adjust. Scatter cilantro over the top. Serve immediately over steamed rice.
